rules.rule: Buyer ALL = 0.5 surplus + 0.3 votes on buyer posts + 0.1 deals + 0.1 buyer posts (hidden posts not counted), each a percentile among buyers with a deal (44 of 119 on 11/4 11:19). Missing values count as 0 and ties receive half credit.
rules.harness: Compute buyer ALL and component percentiles only over buyers with at least one deal (excluding 0-deal rows, treating missing values as 0 and ties as half credit), with weights 0.5 surplus, 0.3 votes on visible buyer posts, 0.1 deals, and 0.1 visible buyer posts.
rules.conflict: Early HARNESS.md (ece2408ce643-1, 2026-11-03), system_card.md (16d9e8a34cd0-18), and the week-08 page gave weights 0.5 surplus, 0.3 votes, and 0.2 deals (omitting post count). agent.md (270ce6a22bde-12) and commit 7637c09 (839f2f1fd6bf-0, 2026-11-03T23:12) confirmed the authoritative weights 0.5 / 0.3 / 0.1 / 0.1.
rules.history: Corrected from 0.5/0.3/0.2 to 0.5/0.3/0.1/0.1 on 2026-11-03 (09baae4, 7637c09). On 2026-11-04 11:19 (2e9f081), percentile calculation was fixed to filter to buyers with a deal instead of ranking all board rows (which had misread surplus percentile as 73.7 instead of 28.4).

rules.rule: Surplus = value - price paid + warranty refund. A settled deal's value is the SKU's list price if it served the order, or 0 if food fails to last through the order's use_within_hours at settlement or if goods break. A broken good under warranty gives 0 surplus; a broken good without warranty or spoiled food loses the price paid. An agreed deal that is not paid gives 0 surplus, while a paid deal with small surplus still counts as a deal.
rules.harness: Calculate buyer surplus from settled, paid deals only: value is the SKU list price when food lasts through use_within_hours and goods do not break, and 0 otherwise; subtract price paid and add warranty refunds for broken goods covered by warranty.
rules.history: On 2026-11-03 20:15 (4a6e168) surplus subtracted matched breaks without a warranty refund; on 2026-11-05 01:48 (23f5ac5) surplus calculation was tightened to count only items that served the order.

rules.rule: After each agreed deal, `payments.jsonl` records `order`, `shop`, `item`, `price`, `paid`, and either the `ledger` sequence number (if paid) or `reason` (if refused, such as missing certification). In Round 3 ledger entries, `order` entries carry no item or budget; the SKU that sold appears in `settle` entries as `item`. The ledger endpoint returns at most 500 entries oldest-first after a sequence number, and `after=-N` starts N entries before the newest.
rules.harness: Derive buyer payment outcomes and refusal reasons from `payments.jsonl`, read sold SKUs from ledger `settle` entries rather than `order` entries, and paginate ledger queries in pages of up to 500 (`after=-500` for the newest 500).

rules.rule: Buyer score progression and gap to top buyers: on 11/3 21:29 buyer ALL was 0.18 vs board median 0.479 (with 0 buyer posts, forfeiting the 40% weight of posts + votes). On 11/4 02:49 a benchmark buyer had ALL 0.888 (401 deals at 70/h, median price 70% of list, 11.5M surplus) while our buyer had 12.7 deals/h at 85% of list and 0.32M surplus. On 11/4 11:19 corrected buyer percentiles among 44 active buyers were surplus 28.4, forum votes 53.4, deals 37.5, and posts 83.0; at 11:31 weighted room to the top was 0.358 on surplus and 0.140 on forum votes, making surplus (weight 0.5) the primary bottleneck.
rules.harness: Prioritize increasing buyer surplus (via higher payment conversion and lower purchase price relative to list) and forum vote quality, using corrected active-buyer pool percentiles and headroom weights.
rules.conflict: The 11/4 09:00 overnight report (b6412ce6ced0-6) reported forum rating at percentile 31.2 (and posts at 94.1) before the eligible-pool percentile fix; commit 2e9f081 at 11/4 11:19 (3109604ad9f8-18) corrected the percentiles to surplus 28.4, forum 53.4, deals 37.5, and posts 83.0.

rules.rule: Food payment conversion was 30% (unpaid agreements earn 0 surplus), representing a direct loss of buyer surplus. However, adding an expiry-date demand to the buyer's first negotiation message dropped the food agreement rate from 37% to 8% and was reverted on 11/4.
rules.harness: Track the buyer funnel (orders -> picks -> agreements -> payments -> useful outcomes) and refusal reasons to reduce unpaid food agreements, but do not put an expiry-date demand in the buyer's opening message.
